text:
Sophie (sales): FYI — ACME InfoSec/Legal sent a vendor security/privacy packet for the POC. They asked for: SIG/CAIQ export, data flow diagram for the POC, retention/deletion proof, DSAR handling steps, encryption details, and a list of subprocessors. Need a turnaround by EOD Wed. Can we hit that?

Ethan (security): We can assemble SIG/CAIQ answers fast — I have a baseline doc. For encryption: TLS1.2+ for in-transit, AES-256 for at-rest by default (KMS-managed keys).

Maya (eng): For the POC we'll spin up a sandbox in the dedicated cluster (no external logs forwarded). Dataflow will be: customer app -> API gateway (NAT) -> POC runtime (ephemeral GPUs) -> KV cache (encrypted) -> optional S3 for artifacts. I can draw a diagram and attach.

Lucas (legal): Quick notes from legal: they want DPA language (standard Redmond clause + security measures) and confirmation of SCCs/adequacy approach. Also need the DSAR point of contact and evidence we can delete customer data on request (not just stop processing).

Aisha (solutions): POC specifics — we usually recommend synthetic or redacted data, but if they insist on real data we require an approved MOU + strict retention window. Proposed POC retention: 30 days by default, auto-delete after 30d. Can we script a proof-of-deletion artefact?

Ethan (security): Yes — we can provide a deletion runbook and a signed deletion token. Proposed proof-of-deletion flow: 1) run DB delete job, 2) run S3 lifecycle purge + version clean, 3) export manifest of deleted IDs + hash, 4) capture job logs + timestamped signature. Example SQL snippet for deletion: 
```sql
BEGIN;
DELETE FROM poc_inputs WHERE customer_id = 'acme-123';
-- VACUUM or OPTIMIZE depending on DB
COMMIT;
```

Maya (eng): For S3 we use lifecycle + explicit expunge for versions. Example lifecycle snippet (for their reading):
```xml
<LifecycleConfiguration>
  <Rule>
    <ID>POC-expunge</ID>
    <Status>Enabled</Status>
    <Expiration><Days>30</Days></Expiration>
  </Rule>
</LifecycleConfiguration>
```

Sophie (sales): Good. Can someone own the SIG/CAIQ Q&A and the dataflow diagram? I'll consolidate and send to the buyer. Also they asked about subprocessors list — please confirm the current vendors we disclose.

Ethan (security): I'll take SIG/CAIQ and subprocessor check. Current subprocessors (to disclose): cloud infra provider (GCP-us-east4), metrics/telemetry provider (Datadog), S3-compatible blob store (internal partner), KMS provider (cloud KMS). I'll prepare a short CSV.

Lucas (legal): I'll draft the DPA paragraph and SCCs approach. Note: if they require EU SCCs plus UK addendum we have a standard exhibit — I'll attach it. Also we should confirm our DSAR SLA (we usually commit 30 days to complete an identification+remediation proof).

Aisha (solutions): For the POC environment I propose these constraints we tell the customer: no external webhook callbacks, IP allowlist, disable exports, and an automated deletion job scheduled at the end of the POC. I can add these to the POC checklist.

Redwood-bot: Task created — #task-4281 "ACME POC security packet" assigned to Ethan, Maya, Lucas. Due: 1769214290 (2026-08-01).

Maya (eng): I'll attach a quick ASCII dataflow for the initial send until I can produce a diagram:

customer -> nginx (ingress, TLS) -> auth layer (tokenized) -> runtime (ephemeral, no persistent mounts) -> encrypted cache -> optional s3 (encrypted, versioned)

Ethan (security): Also callout: KV cache keys are zeroed on pod termination in the POC (we'll add a lifecycle hook). Add note that telemetry logs are sampled and scrub PII fields by default (names, emails).

Sophie (sales): Perfect — timeline: Ethan: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor CSV by EOD today. Maya: dataflow diagram + deletion proof example by tomorrow morning. Lucas: DPA + SCC comment by tomorrow afternoon. I'll assemble and send to buyer Wed morning.

Lucas (legal): One more: for DSARs specify our contact email privacy@example.redwood.com and include a runbook excerpt: what we provide (confirmation of processing, categories, recipients, retention, and deletion certification).

Aisha (solutions): I'll prep a short FAQ for the buyer about what we can and can't delete (backups, logs retention windows) and the expected delay for complete purging.

Sophie (sales): Thanks team. I'll ping if they push back on retention length. If they require shorter than 30d we'll need a security sign-off for nightly deletion jobs and a pricing note (extra ops).

Ethan (security): Noted — shorter windows for real data incur monitoring/ops overhead. We should pre-approve a run rate for accelerated deletion as an add-on.

Sophie (sales): Added to the checklist. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Redwood-bot: Reminder set for 1769170000 (24h before due).
